 Diwali 2026 falls on November 8, not November 9. Check the correct date as per Hindu Panchang, Lakshmi Puja muhurat, Amavasya Tithi and city-wise auspicious timings.

 Lakshmi Puja muhurat in New Delhi is from 5:54 pm to 7:50 pm.
 Amavasya falls during Pradosh Kaal on November 8.

 Diwali 2026 will be celebrated in India on Sunday, November 8, and not November 9. As the festival of lights approaches, the question of the correct date has surfaced among families preparing for Lakshmi Puja, festive gatherings and traditional celebrations. The confusion stems from the Amavasya Tithi, which begins on November 8 and continues until the afternoon of November 9. 
 According to the Hindu Panchang, Diwali is observed on Kartik Amavasya, the new moon day of the lunar month of Kartik. However, the festival date is determined by the presence of Amavasya during the evening Pradosh Kaal, when Lakshmi Puja is traditionally performed. In 2026, this auspicious period falls on November 8. 
 For devotees in New Delhi, the main Lakshmi Puja muhurat will be from 5:54 pm to 7:50 pm. Here is a detailed look at the correct Diwali date, Tithi timings, puja muhurat and the festival calendar for 2026. 
 Is Diwali 2026 on November 8 or November 9? 
 Diwali 2026 will be observed on Sunday, November 8, across India. November 9 is not the main Diwali celebration date, even though Amavasya Tithi continues into that day.  According to Drik Panchang, the Amavasya Tithi begins at 11:27 am on November 8 and ends at 12:31 pm on November 9. Since Amavasya prevails during the evening Pradosh Kaal on November 8, that date is considered appropriate for Lakshmi Puja. 
 On November 9, the Amavasya Tithi will end around noon, well before sunset. Therefore, the evening Lakshmi Puja associated with Diwali will be observed on November 8. 
 Why is there confusion over Diwali 2026 date? 
 The difference between the Hindu lunar calendar and the Gregorian calendar is the primary reason for the confusion.  Unlike the calendar followed on smartphones and everyday schedules, the Hindu Panchang is based on lunar phases and Tithis. A Tithi does not necessarily begin or end at midnight. It can extend across two Gregorian dates, making a festival appear to fall on more than one day. 
 In 2026, Amavasya begins on November 8 and ends on November 9. This overlap has led to questions about whether Diwali should be celebrated on November 8 or November 9.  The key factor is the timing of Lakshmi Puja. Since Amavasya is present during Pradosh Kaal on November 8, the festival is observed on that day. 
 Diwali 2026 Lakshmi Puja Muhurat and Shubh Timings 
 Lakshmi Puja is the most important religious observance of Diwali. Devotees worship Goddess Lakshmi, Lord Ganesha and Goddess Saraswati, seeking blessings for prosperity, wisdom, happiness and well-being.  As per Drik Panchang, the Lakshmi Puja muhurat for New Delhi on November 8 is as follows: 
 Event Date and Timing 
 Diwali 2026 Sunday, November 8 
 Lakshmi Puja Muhurat 5:54 pm to 7:50 pm 
 Duration 1 hour 56 minutes 
 Pradosh Kaal 5:31 pm to 8:09 pm 
 Vrishabha Kaal 5:54 pm to 7:50 pm 
 Amavasya Tithi Begins 11:27 am, November 8 
 Amavasya Tithi Ends 12:31 pm, November 9 
 The Lakshmi Puja window falls within Pradosh Kaal and Vrishabha Kaal, both considered auspicious for the evening worship. 
 City-wise Lakshmi Puja Muhurat for Diwali 2026 
 Lakshmi Puja timings vary from city to city due to differences in local sunset timings. Devotees should follow the muhurat prescribed for their location. 
 City Lakshmi Puja Muhurat 
 Kolkata 5:20 pm to 7:18 pm 
 New Delhi 5:54 pm to 7:50 pm 
 Gurgaon 5:55 pm to 7:51 pm 
 Chandigarh 5:52 pm to 7:46 pm 
 Jaipur 6:03 pm to 7:59 pm 
 Chennai 6:07 pm to 8:09 pm 
 Hyderabad 6:07 pm to 8:08 pm 
 Bengaluru 6:17 pm to 8:20 pm 
 Pune 6:24 pm to 8:24 pm 
 Mumbai 6:27 pm to 8:27 pm 
 Ahmedabad 6:22 pm to 8:20 pm 
 Noida 5:54 pm to 7:49 pm 
 All timings are local to the respective cities. 
 Diwali 2026: Complete festival dates and calendar 
 Diwali is celebrated over several days, with each observance carrying its own religious and cultural significance. The 2026 festival calendar includes Dhanteras, Naraka Chaturdashi, Lakshmi Puja, Govardhan Puja and Bhai Dooj. 
 Festival Date Day 
 Dhanteras November 6, 2026 Friday 
 Naraka Chaturdashi / Choti Diwali November 8, 2026 Sunday 
 Diwali / Lakshmi Puja November 8, 2026 Sunday 
 Govardhan Puja November 9, 2026 Monday 
 Bhai Dooj November 11, 2026 Wednesday 
 Naraka Chaturdashi and Diwali coincide on November 8 this year. The pre-dawn Abhyanga Snan associated with Naraka Chaturdashi and the evening Lakshmi Puja will both be observed on the same date. 
 How is Lakshmi Puja performed on Diwali? 
 Lakshmi Puja is traditionally performed after sunset during the auspicious evening muhurat. Homes are cleaned and decorated with flowers, rangoli and diyas ahead of the ritual.  The puja generally begins with the worship of Lord Ganesha, who is invoked for the removal of obstacles. Goddess Lakshmi is then worshipped for wealth and prosperity, while Goddess Saraswati is revered for knowledge and wisdom. 
 Devotees offer flowers, fruits, sweets, incense and lamps to the deities. Many families also worship their business account books, valuables and household possessions as a prayer for financial stability and success. 
 The evening is marked by the lighting of diyas, prayers, the exchange of sweets and festive greetings. For many households, Lakshmi Puja is the spiritual heart of Diwali, bringing families together to welcome prosperity and new beginnings. 
 Diwali 2026: What devotees should remember 
 Diwali 2026 will be celebrated on November 8, despite Amavasya Tithi extending into November 9. The evening presence of Amavasya on November 8 determines the main Lakshmi Puja date. 
 Devotees planning their celebrations should check the city-specific muhurat, as the auspicious timings differ across locations. With the correct date and puja window established, families can prepare for the festival without confusion and observe the traditional rituals on the appropriate day.
